agent_notes: The fix follows an existing pattern. refresh_radarr_counts (engine.py:1953, 1982) and refresh_lidarr_counts (engine.py:2281, 2305) already call filter_monitored right after the first key-field screen and before any date or tag screen. All three refresh helpers now use the same order as their run_*_cycle counterparts.

In the cutoff chain, cutoff_screened stays as the output of the first key-field screen only. filter_monitored now writes to filtered_cutoff, so the value the helper returns (per the comment, 'cutoff_screened is also what the tuple returns') still holds monitored and unmonitored records. That matches what it returned before the reorder: the old code also returned cutoff_screened before the monitored filter. No contract change.

Already true before this diff, not introduced by it: refresh_sonarr_counts repeats the screen → monitored → date-screen → filter_sonarr_episodes → tag-screen → filter_by_tag → key-screen → deduplicate_to_seasons chain from run_sonarr_cycle almost line for line, and the Radarr and Lidarr pairs do the same. Two copies of this chain per app is exactly why the order drifted (WR-01). A shared per-app filter-chain helper would stop that drift. This diff only lines the copies up and adds no new copy, so under the rule of three it is not a finding.

The new test is in tests/test_refresh_counts.py and uses the file's existing helpers (_make_sonarr_episode, _make_test_state, make_settings, _instance_config) and its add-then-remove loguru sink pattern with try/finally. It is consistent with the neighbouring tests.
There are no new imports or dependencies and no cross-module coupling changes. filter_monitored is defined in engine.py itself (line 288).

The cutoff tuple return still yields cutoff_screened, the list from before the monitored filter. That behaviour predates this diff and the diff does not change it.

The new test's assertion `"malformed date" not in sink.getvalue()` is not vacuous. _malformed_reason returns "date" for a date with no timezone (engine.py:149-152), and _log_malformed_skip prints "malformed {key} data", so without the fix the log would contain "malformed date data" and the test would fail.

Scope: two lines change in refresh_sonarr_counts (triggarr/search/engine.py:2112 and :2139–2141). Both add filter_monitored() between the first record-shape _screen_queue pass and the airDateUtc date screen, on the missing chain and the cutoff chain. One parametrized regression test is added in tests/test_refresh_counts.py.

Parity: the refresh chain now runs its steps in the same order as run_sonarr_cycle (engine.py:1368–1372 for missing, :1415–1419 for cutoff): shape screen, filter_monitored, airDateUtc screen, filter_sonarr_episodes, tag screen and filter, key screen, dedup. That closes the earlier difference between the refresh path and the scheduled path.

Count semantics do not change. filter_sonarr_episodes (engine.py:426–451) already drops any episode whose monitored flag is not set to true. So filtering unmonitored records earlier only changes which records reach the airDateUtc screen. An unmonitored episode with a timezone-less or malformed air date is now dropped quietly instead of being logged as a skipped malformed record. missing_eligible, missing_searchable and cutoff_searchable come out the same for every input.

Return value unchanged: the function still returns cutoff_screened, the list after the first shape screen only, before filter_monitored. Whatever consumes that tuple in triggarr/web/routes.py:1163 (the refresh dispatch table) gets the same data as before. The new filtered_cutoff local is assigned first by filter_monitored and then overwritten by the date screen, so no variable scoping changes.

Type safety: filter_monitored calls item.get, and its input has already been through the shape _screen_queue pass, which skips records that are not objects (D-02). No new AttributeError path reaches the (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError) backstop at engine.py:2170.

Blast radius: limited to the manual Refresh-counts action for Sonarr instances, reached through routes.py. No public signature, state schema or persisted-field change. Radarr and Lidarr refresh paths (engine.py:1953/1982 and 2281/2305) already had this order and are untouched. Performance: adds one O(n) list comprehension per queue, which is negligible next to the HTTP fetch.

Test: the new parametrized test checks both the missing and the cutoff queue. In each, an unmonitored episode with a timezone-less airDateUtc must produce no 'malformed date' warning, the instance must stay connected, and missing_eligible must be 1. That pins the fix on both changed lines.
Verdict: shippable as-is; no blocking impact.

findings.title: Sonarr Refresh counts: the missing-queue tag-filter step never runs in any test
findings.problem: When a tag is set for Sonarr's missing queue, Refresh counts takes an extra step: it checks each episode's series tags and keeps only the matching ones. No test turns that step on. The coverage report shows the check at L2117 always going the same way, and the tag-screening and tag-filtering lines at L2118 and L2122 never run. The fix in this change reorders the steps just above it, so the tag path now gets different input than before and nothing has checked it.
findings.fix_hint: Add a Sonarr refresh test with a missing-queue tag configured: one matching episode, one non-matching episode, and one record with malformed series tags. Assert the eligible count and that the instance stays connected.
findings.why_it_matters: Tag-scoped counts are what the dashboard shows for users who limit searches by tag. If this path breaks, Sonarr could show wrong counts or disconnect the instance over one bad record, and no test would catch it. The cutoff side of the same code is tested, so the missing side is the gap.

findings.title: No test checks that Refresh counts returns the cleaned cutoff list, not the raw one
findings.problem: Radarr's Refresh counts returns the cutoff list after bad records have been removed (`cutoff_screened`), so callers never receive a malformed item. The return line runs in tests, but the only test that checks the returned cutoff list (tests/test_refresh_counts.py:655) uses all-valid records. The cleaned list and the raw list are identical there, so a change back to returning the raw list would still pass.
findings.current_code: return (filtered_missing, cutoff_screened if not scope.cutoff_unresolved else [], scope.cutoff_tag_id)
findings.fix_hint: Add a refresh test with one malformed cutoff record and assert the returned cutoff list leaves it out.
findings.why_it_matters: This return value is the only thing stopping a malformed record from reaching the code that uses the cutoff list. If it quietly went back to the raw list, the crash this phase fixes could come back somewhere else, with no failing test to warn about it.

findings.title: New cutoff-variant test only checks the missing-queue count, not the cutoff counts
findings.problem: The new test runs twice, once per queue. In the cutoff run, the unmonitored episode is only in the cutoff queue, but the test only checks the missing-queue count and that no 'malformed date' warning was logged. It never checks that the cutoff count leaves out the unmonitored episode.
findings.current_code:
assert ist["missing_eligible"] == 1
assert "malformed date" not in sink.getvalue()
findings.fix_hint: In the cutoff run, also assert the cutoff searchable count is 0.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix adds the monitored-only filter to both queues. This test proves the warning is gone, but on the cutoff side it does not prove the count is right.
